before_step.derivation: Let a state after k rounds be S_k=(R_k,B_k,G_k), with nonnegative integer counts. Initially S_0=(3,2,1), so the total is N_0=3+2+1=6. For any state (r,b,g), put N=r+b+g. A uniform draw gives color probabilities proportional to the current counts: P(red | (r,b,g))=r/N, P(blue | (r,b,g))=b/N, and P(green | (r,b,g))=g/N. The update rules then determine the next state. If red is drawn, the red ball is returned and one blue ball is added, so (r,b,g) goes to (r,b+1,g). If blue is drawn, the blue ball is removed and one green ball is added, so (r,b,g) goes to (r,b-1,g+1). If green is drawn, the green ball is returned and one red ball is added, so (r,b,g) goes to (r+1,b,g). Thus one round has a state-dependent transition kernel. The total changes by +1 on red or green draws and stays the same on a blue draw, because blue is removed and green is added. This step only fixes notation and the transition rules; it does not evaluate any multi-round probability.
before_step.result: State S=(r,b,g); initial state S0=(3,2,1). One-round transitions: red with prob r/(r+b+g) to (r,b+1,g); blue with prob b/(r+b+g) to (r,b-1,g+1); green with prob g/(r+b+g) to (r+1,b,g).

plan_step.goal: Define state (r,b,g), total n, draw probabilities r/n, b/n, g/n, and the one-round update maps; record the initial state (3,2,1).

returned_step.derivation: Let S_k=(R_k,B_k,G_k) be the urn after k rounds. The initial state is S_0=(3,2,1), since the urn begins with 3 red, 2 blue, and 1 green ball; hence N_0=3+2+1=6. For any state S=(r,b,g) reached during the six rounds, let N=r+b+g. Since draws are uniform over the current urn, the conditional draw probabilities are P(red | S)=r/N, P(blue | S)=b/N, and P(green | S)=g/N. The update rule from a red draw returns the red ball and adds one blue ball, so r is unchanged, b increases by 1, and g is unchanged: (r,b,g)->(r,b+1,g). The update rule from a blue draw removes that blue ball and adds one green ball, so r is unchanged, b decreases by 1, and g increases by 1: (r,b,g)->(r,b-1,g+1), with this transition available only when b>0. The update rule from a green draw returns the green ball and adds one red ball, so r increases by 1, b is unchanged, and g is unchanged: (r,b,g)->(r+1,b,g). The total becomes N+1 after red or green, and remains N after blue, since blue is replaced by green. This step fixes notation and the one-round transition kernel; it does not evaluate six-round probabilities.
